newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 13.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc have agreed to merge in a deal worth about $22.27 billion.
* Delta Air Lines Inc Chairman, Chief Executive and President Ronald Allen said he plans to retire this summer.
* The U.S. Supreme Court has ruled that companies cannot lay off employees solely to reduce the cost of providing health care and other benefits.
* Panamerican Beverages Inc has merged with Coca-Cola Hit de Venezuela for about $1.01 billion in stock and cash, plus $108.6 million of assumed debt.
* The Dow Jones Industrials rose 123.22 points to a record 7292.75.
* U.S. grain stocks are likely to be replenished this fall by farmers who are harvesting bumper crops of corn and soybean.
* The U.S. Transportation Department is set to pave the way for more low-fare airlines to get lucrative take-off rights at some large airports.
* The U.S. Labor Department is preparing a proposal to ask states to extend unemployment compensation to part-time workers and those who quit their jobs.
* Wal-Mart Stores Inc reported a 14 percent increase in net income for the first quarter.
* Paxson Communications Corp has agreed to acquire WBIS+, a New York television station, from Dow Jones & Co Inc and ITT Corp.
* News Corp Ltd has reached a tentative deal to buy the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team for about $350 million, according to unnamed sources.
* Seagram Co Ltd's Universal Pictures studio plans to double movie production by 2000.
* Apple Computer Inc is seeking to assure software developers that its future operating system will also run on the current Macintosh system.
* Lipper has agreed to publish data on mutual funds that includes pre-inception performance.
* Heard on the Street: Tony Blair, Britain's new prime minister, isn't considered the same kind of threat to markets as were some of his more extreme Labor Party predecessors.

* Credit markets: Bonds edged marginally higher yesterday on assumptions that economic and inflation data this week will show a slowing economy, allowing the Federal Reserve to hold off an interest-rate increase on May 20.
